Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred while the patient was
changing lanes. Imaging confirmed a distal radius fracture of the wrist, and the
mechanism described is consistent with the injury observed. The patient has no known
prior injury to the same area. Over the course of care, the patient attended 19 visits,
which is somewhat longer than typically expected for a fracture of this type.
Examination findings include tenderness and reduced grip strength on the affected side
that support the diagnosis, while neurovascular tseting and range-of-motion results on
the unaffected joints were within normal limits. Immobilization was followed by
graduated physical therapy, and progress has been steady though slower than
anticipated. Billed services reflect the treatment delivered, with no repeated or
duplicate charges identified in the record. Ongoing monitoring and a home exercise
program are planned.
